questions.question: Trichomonads are flagellate protozoa possessing how many anterior flagella?
questions.explanation: Trichomonads possess three to five anterior flagella — one of the features used to classify them within the family Trichomonadidae.

questions.question: Members of the family Trichomonadidae are found in intestinal or reproductive tracts of vertebrates and invertebrates, with one group living exclusively in the gut of what?
questions.explanation: One group of trichomonads lives exclusively in the gut of termites, where they help digest cellulose — a mutualistic association.

questions.question: How many trichomonad species are common in humans?
questions.explanation: Three trichomonad species are common in humans: T. tenax (mouth), T. hominis (intestine), and T. vaginalis (urogenital tract).

questions.question: Which Trichomonas species causes the most common form of trichomoniasis in humans?
questions.explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis causes the most common form of trichomoniasis in humans — a sexually transmitted infection of the urogenital tract.

questions.question: Trichomonas tenax was first discovered by whom?
questions.explanation: Trichomonas tenax was first discovered by O.F. Müller in 1773 — one of the earliest described trichomonads.

questions.question: In which year was Trichomonas tenax first discovered?
questions.explanation: O.F. Müller discovered T. tenax in 1773 — more than a century before the other human trichomonads were identified.

questions.question: Trichomonas tenax possesses how many anterior flagella?
questions.explanation: T. tenax possesses four anterior flagella — a distinguishing morphological feature.

questions.question: The fifth flagellum of T. tenax curves back along the margin of what?
questions.explanation: The fifth flagellum of T. tenax curves back along the margin of an undulating membrane — the same pattern seen in other trichomonads.

questions.question: Trichomonas tenax has been found only in which part of the human body?
questions.explanation: T. tenax has been found only in the human mouth — specifically in the tartar between teeth, in gums, and in tooth cavities.

questions.question: Trichomonas tenax is considered to be what?
questions.explanation: T. tenax is considered a harmless commensal of the mouth. It does not cause disease and is only noted because it can be mistaken for other trichomonads.

questions.question: Transmission of T. tenax is direct, usually through what?
options: Kissing or common use of utensils
questions.explanation: Transmission of T. tenax is direct, usually through kissing or common use of utensils — habits that pass oral secretions from person to person.

questions.question: Trophozoites of T. tenax divide by what process?
questions.explanation: Trophozoites of T. tenax divide by binary fission. No cyst stage is known for this species.

questions.question: Trichomonas tenax is most abundant between the teeth and gums and in what else?
questions.explanation: T. tenax is most abundant between the teeth and gums, and in pus pockets around teeth and in tooth cavities — environments rich in organic debris.

questions.question: Trichomonas hominis was discovered by whom?
questions.explanation: Trichomonas hominis was discovered by Davaine, who named it Cercomonas hominis in 1860.

questions.question: In which year did Davaine name the organism Cercomonas hominis?
questions.explanation: Davaine named the organism Cercomonas hominis in 1860. It was later reclassified into the genus Trichomonas.

questions.question: Trichomonas hominis is a harmless commensal of which organ?
questions.explanation: T. hominis is a harmless commensal of the large intestine. It does not invade tissue or cause disease.

questions.question: Trichomonas hominis is the most common intestinal flagellate of humans after which organism?
questions.explanation: T. hominis is the most common intestinal flagellate of humans after Giardia intestinalis. Both are found worldwide.

questions.question: Which stage of Trichomonas hominis is known?
questions.explanation: Only the trophozoite stage of T. hominis is known. No cyst stage has been identified — transmission is by direct transfer of trophozoites.

questions.question: The trophozoite of Trichomonas hominis is described as what shape?
questions.explanation: The trophozoite of T. hominis is pear-shaped (pyriform), with a rounded anterior end and tapering posterior end.

questions.question: The flagella arrangement in T. hominis is referred to as what?
questions.explanation: The flagella arrangement in T. hominis is four-plus-one — four anterior flagella plus one that curves along the undulating membrane.

questions.question: Trichomonas hominis divides by what process?
questions.explanation: T. hominis divides by longitudinal binary fission — the plane of division runs lengthwise, producing two identical daughter cells.

questions.question: In formed stools, Trichomonas hominis are rounded and dormant but not what?
questions.explanation: In formed stools, T. hominis trophozoites become rounded and dormant, but they are not truly encysted — they lack a cyst wall. They resume activity when conditions improve.

questions.question: Flies associated with filth can serve as what for T. hominis?
questions.explanation: Flies associated with filth can serve as mechanical vectors for T. hominis — they carry trophozoites on their bodies and deposit them on food.

questions.question: Diagnosis of T. hominis depends on identification of the organism in what?
questions.explanation: Diagnosis of T. hominis depends on identification of the trophozoite in faecal preparations — fresh wet mounts examined microscopically.

questions.question: Trichomonas vaginalis was first found by whom?
questions.explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis was first found by Donne in 1836 in the vaginal secretions of a woman with vaginitis.

questions.question: In which year was Trichomonas vaginalis first found?
questions.explanation: Donne discovered T. vaginalis in 1836 — a full 60 years before it was recognised as the cause of trichomoniasis.

questions.question: Trichomonas vaginalis is found inhabiting which tracts?
questions.explanation: T. vaginalis inhabits the reproductive tracts of both sexes — vagina, cervix, and urethra in women; prostate, seminal vesicles, and urethra in men.

questions.question: In women, T. vaginalis lives in the vagina, vulva, cervix, and what else?
questions.explanation: In women, T. vaginalis lives in the vagina, vulva, cervix, and urethra — the entire lower urogenital tract.

questions.question: In men, T. vaginalis lives in the prostate, seminal vesicles, and what else?
questions.explanation: In men, T. vaginalis lives in the prostate, seminal vesicles, and urethra — often asymptomatically, which is why men are important carriers.

questions.question: Trichomonas vaginalis is transmitted primarily by what?
questions.explanation: T. vaginalis is transmitted primarily by sexual intercourse. It is one of the most common sexually transmitted infections worldwide.

questions.question: The acidity of normal vagina is what pH range?
questions.explanation: The normal vaginal pH is 3.8 to 4.5 — maintained by lactic acid-producing bacteria (Lactobacillus). This acidity protects against many pathogens.

questions.question: Once established, T. vaginalis causes a shift toward what?
questions.explanation: Once established, T. vaginalis causes a shift toward alkalinity — the parasite consumes the lactobacilli and produces its own metabolic products that raise pH.

questions.question: The pH shift caused by T. vaginalis is to what range?
questions.explanation: The pH shift caused by T. vaginalis is to a range of 5 to 6 — much less acidic, allowing other pathogens to flourish and producing the characteristic symptoms.

questions.question: Trichomoniasis is a chronic infection of which tract?
questions.explanation: Trichomoniasis is a chronic infection of the genital tract. It can persist for years if untreated.

questions.question: In the female, trichomoniasis presents with vaginitis accompanied by what?
questions.explanation: In the female, trichomoniasis presents with vaginitis accompanied by copious discharge — typically thin, frothy, yellow-green, and foul-smelling.

questions.question: Trichomoniasis is caused by which organism?
questions.explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by Trichomonas vaginalis — the urogenital trichomonad. The other species cause no disease in humans.

questions.question: The incubation period of trichomoniasis is how long?
questions.explanation: The incubation period of trichomoniasis is 1 to 3 weeks, though some infections remain asymptomatic for much longer.

questions.question: A few days after infection, there is degeneration of vaginal epithelium followed by infiltration by what?
questions.explanation: A few days after infection, there is degeneration of vaginal epithelium followed by infiltration by leucocytes — the immune response that produces the heavy discharge.

questions.question: The vaginal secretions in trichomoniasis become abundant and white, a condition known as what?
questions.explanation: The vaginal secretions in trichomoniasis become abundant and white, a condition known as leucorrhoea — the classical presenting complaint.

questions.question: Signs and symptoms in females with trichomoniasis include vulvae pruritis and what else?
questions.explanation: Signs and symptoms in females include vulval pruritus (itching) and a burning sensation — especially during urination and intercourse.

questions.question: In men, trichomoniasis is usually what?
questions.explanation: In men, trichomoniasis is usually asymptomatic. Men act as silent carriers who reinfect their partners — a key reason simultaneous treatment is required.

questions.question: Diagnosis of trichomoniasis depends on examination of what?
options: Wet film preparation of vaginal or urethral secretions
questions.explanation: Diagnosis depends on examination of wet film preparations of vaginal or urethral secretions — motile trophozoites are seen under the microscope.

questions.question: Which drug usually cures trichomoniasis in about five days?
questions.explanation: Metronidazole usually cures trichomoniasis in about five days — it is the drug of choice, well tolerated and highly effective.

questions.question: Which drugs are equally effective as metronidazole with fewer side effects?
questions.explanation: Tinidazole and ornidazole are equally effective as metronidazole with fewer side effects — they have longer half-lives and can be given in single doses.

questions.question: Postmenopausal patients may require treatment with what to improve vaginal epithelium?
questions.explanation: Postmenopausal patients may require treatment with estrogens — low estrogen thins the vaginal epithelium, making it more vulnerable. Estrogen restores thickness.

questions.question: The reservoir of trichomoniasis infection is exclusively in what?
questions.explanation: The reservoir of trichomoniasis is exclusively in humans. No animal reservoir exists — T. vaginalis is anthroponotic.

questions.question: Infants may be infected with T. vaginalis during what?
questions.explanation: Infants may be infected during birth — they can acquire T. vaginalis from an infected mother's birth canal, though the infection often clears spontaneously.

questions.question: Control of T. vaginalis infections always requires simultaneous treatment of whom?
questions.explanation: Control always requires simultaneous treatment of both sexual partners — otherwise the untreated partner reinfects the treated one.

questions.question: Mechanical protection during intercourse until infection is eradicated is provided by what?
questions.explanation: Mechanical protection during intercourse is provided by a condom. It prevents transmission of T. vaginalis and other STIs while treatment is completed.

questions.question: Trichomoniasis has what type of distribution?
questions.explanation: Trichomoniasis has a worldwide distribution — it is one of the most common non-viral sexually transmitted infections globally.
